question: A 66-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of constipation and streaks of blood in his stool. He has had a 10-kg (22-lb) weight loss during this period. Colonoscopy shows an exophytic tumor in the sigmoid colon. A CT scan of the abdomen shows liver metastases and enlarged mesenteric and para-aortic lymph nodes. A diagnosis of stage IV colorectal cancer is made, and palliative chemotherapy is initiated. The chemotherapy regimen includes a monoclonal antibody that inhibits tumor growth by preventing ligand binding to a protein directly responsible for epithelial cell proliferation and organogenesis. Which of the following proteins is most likely inhibited by this drug?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Monoclonal antibody inhibits ligand binding" -> "Prevents activation of downstream signaling pathway" -> "Inhibits tumor growth" -> "Directly targets protein involved in cell proliferation and organogenesis" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Monoclonal antibody inhibits ligand binding" -> "Blocks activation of growth factor receptor" -> "Inhibits tumor growth" -> "Targets protein involved in cell proliferation and organogenesis" -> 90%
analysis: The drug described in the scenario that inhibits tumor growth by preventing ligand binding to a protein directly responsible for epithelial cell proliferation and organogenesis is most likely targeting the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR). EGFR is a key protein involved in cell growth and survival, and its overexpression is commonly seen in colorectal cancer.
